title: Dedicated leaky-bucket quota with hosted backfill quarantine
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: When dedicated capacity saturates in a region or tier, naive spillover to hosted can cause noisy neighbor scenarios and large cost spikes for tenants. Current spillover has limited isolation: hosted requests are accepted immediately causing token bursts and downstream QoS/performance variance. We need a rate-limited quarantine mechanism that preserves tenant affinity to dedicated lanes, enforces soft quotas, and uses model-variant demotion and regional remapping as fallback.

Goal: Implement a leaky-bucket style quota allocator at the tenant-region-tier level that: 1) gates hosted spillover through a quarantine state when a tenant's dedicated allocation is exhausted, 2) applies progressive variant demotion (quantized/lightweight models) and regional remapping with hysteresis, 3) exposes observability for cost delta, SLO breach risk, and quarantine events, and 4) supports manual override and automated decay policies.

Scope: Server-side routing layer changes (adjudicator + quota engine), runtime admission control hooks, Console UI for quarantine events and override, metrics/logging and a new runbook for evacuation and rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Leaky-bucket quota enforces a per-tenant per-region per-tier spillover threshold and rejects or quarantines requests beyond soft limit
Quarantine transitions visible in Console with timestamped events and rationale
Fallback sequence defined and executed: dedicated -> quarantined-hosted (limited QPS + variant demotion) -> regional remapping -> rejection
No observable token-cost spike > 20% for quarantined tenants under test workload compared to baseline
Automated decay releases quarantine after configured gap with telemetry proving safe rejoin
Playbook documented and validated in chaos test: simulated dedicated eviction triggers quarantine then graceful rollback
implementation_notes:
Design the quota as a leaky-bucket (capacity, leak_rate) keyed by tenant:region:tier. Admissions flow should check: (1) dedicated capacity available -> normal routing, (2) dedicated exhausted -> soft_spill_allowed? if yes move to quarantine lane; if no then initiate immediate fallback. Quarantine lane: throttled QPS, token-budget tracking, instrumented variant flag to switch to quantized model variant or lower-context-length variant. Use existing smart-routing policy service as plugin point. Persist small state in Redis with TTLs and circuit-state metadata; ensure race-free updates via CAS. Add feature flag to rollout gradually.

Trade-offs: Using Redis simplifies rollout but adds single-store dependency; alternative is CRDT in routing layer but longer implementation time. Variant demotion reduces cost but may degrade quality; include per-tenant quality tracking to auto-disable demotion if hallucination/regression occurs.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged internal deploy in staging with 10% of tenants; 2) Canary in a non-critical region for 2 days, increase to 25% tenants; 3) Enable Console notifications and manual override for SRE; 4) Full rollout after 2-week stability window and postmortem; 5) Post-rollout: monitor cost delta, p50/p95 latency, model quality metrics.
